stem: Given the linear sequence ${=t1}\;;\;{=t2}\;;\;{=t3}\;;\;{=t4}\;;\;{=t5}\;;\;\ldots$ determine the common difference.
solution: The common difference is found by subtracting a term from the term that follows it: $d=T_{2}-T_{1}=({=t2})-({=t1})={=d}$.
All of the results are the same, which means we have found the common difference for these numbers: $d={=d}$.
notes: Entry point of the skill, modelled on Q2 (7; 4; 1; -2; -5, d = -3). Half the instances have a negative common difference, so the order of subtraction matters (mc:g10m3s2-1-1:subtracts-earlier-minus-later gives the opposite sign). Numeric family, so no distractors. d is never 0 or a stated 'no common difference' case; every instance is linear and the stem says so.
